source_cards.back: At an eight-sided stop sign, stop completely, yield to other vehicles, and wait for anyone in a marked or unmarked crosswalk; then enter when it is safe.

source_cards.front: What does a triangular yield sign require of you?
source_cards.back: A triangular yield sign means slow down and give the right of way, stopping just as you would at a stop sign if that is needed.

source_cards.front: What does a Left Turn Yield on Green sign require on a green circular light?
source_cards.back: A Left Turn Yield on Green sign means that on a green circular light you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until the turn is safe.

source_cards.front: What does a Right Turns Permitted sign let you do in a transit lane, and how?
source_cards.back: A Right Turns Permitted sign lets you use a transit lane briefly to reach a driveway, the next intersection or legal curb parking; yield to buses and bikes in it and merge in behind them.

source_cards.front: What is the difference between a Crossroad sign and a Side Road sign?
source_cards.back: A Crossroad sign warns of a four-way intersection where cross traffic may enter; a Side Road sign warns of a T intersection with traffic joining from left or right.

source_cards.front: What do the Roundabout Ahead and Railroad Advance signs announce?
source_cards.back: A Roundabout Ahead sign announces a roundabout intersection, and a Railroad Advance sign warns of a railroad crossing where you may need to stop.

source_cards.front: What does a steady circular yellow light warn of, and what should you do?
source_cards.back: A steady circular yellow light warns that red is coming, so stop before the intersection, or if you cannot stop safely, continue carefully through it.

source_cards.front: How does a steady yellow light differ from a steady red light?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow light tells you to stop before the intersection if you safely can, unlike a steady red light, which requires you to stop and stay stopped.

source_cards.front: When may you turn on a flashing yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow allows the turn shown only after you yield to pedestrians and to oncoming traffic, which has a steady green light.

source_cards.front: How does a steady yellow arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected movement is ending, while a flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: What moves does a steady green light allow, and who must turning drivers yield to?
source_cards.back: A steady green light allows straight, left and right moves unless a sign forbids one; left turns yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, right turns yield to pedestrians.

source_cards.front: What does a steady green arrow give you?
source_cards.back: A steady green arrow gives you the right of way to make the movement the arrow shows.

source_cards.front: How does a green arrow differ from a circular green light for a left turn?
source_cards.back: A green arrow gives you the right of way for the movement shown, while a circular green light permits the movement but a left turn must still yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: What does a square Do Not Enter sign tell you, and what does seeing one usually mean?
source_cards.back: A square Do Not Enter sign tells you not to enter that road or freeway, and seeing it usually means you are heading the wrong way.

source_cards.front: What do other regulatory signs look like, and where do they stand?
source_cards.back: Other regulatory signs are rectangles with black words or symbols on white; they tell you what to do and stand at or near the place the rule applies.

source_cards.front: What does a speed limit sign tell you, and can its number change?
source_cards.back: A speed limit sign gives the maximum speed in miles per hour, and electronic versions may change with current conditions.

source_cards.front: What does a Right Turn Permitted Without Stopping sign allow, and what must everyone else do?
source_cards.back: A Right Turn Permitted Without Stopping sign, sometimes under a stop sign, lets right-turning traffic go without stopping while all other traffic must stop and yield.

source_cards.front: What do Do Not Pass and No Turn on Red signs each require?
source_cards.back: A Do Not Pass sign means passing is not allowed, and a No Turn on Red sign means you must wait for the green signal before turning.

source_cards.front: What does a Left Turn Yield on Green sign require on a green circular light?
source_cards.back: A Left Turn Yield on Green sign means that on a green circular light you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until the turn is safe.

source_cards.front: What does a Keep Right sign warn you about, and where should you drive?
source_cards.back: A Keep Right sign warns that an island, median or obstruction splits the road ahead, so you stay to its right.

source_cards.front: What do lane-use control signs tell you at an intersection?
source_cards.back: Lane-use control signs show which lanes must turn or may turn at an intersection.

source_cards.front: Who uses the middle lane marked by a Center Lane Turn Only sign?
source_cards.back: A Center Lane Turn Only sign means the middle lane is shared by left-turning drivers coming from both directions.

source_cards.front: What do yellow warning signs do, and must you react to hazards that have no sign?
source_cards.back: Yellow warning signs flag possible hazards or changed conditions ahead, yet you must react to conditions whether or not a sign warns you.

source_cards.front: Which curve signs warn ahead, and which marks the curve at the sign itself?
source_cards.back: A Curve sign and a Sharp Turn sign warn of what lies ahead, while a Chevron sign marks the sharp curve or direction change at the sign itself.

source_cards.front: How does a Winding Road sign differ from a Reversing Curves sign?
source_cards.back: A Winding Road sign warns of a series of turns or curves, while a Reversing Curves sign warns the road bends right and then left.

source_cards.front: How many curves does a Winding Road sign mean compared with a Reversing Curves sign?
source_cards.back: A Winding Road sign means several turns or curves, while a Reversing Curves sign means one curve right followed by one curve left.

source_cards.front: What is the difference between a Crossroad sign and a Side Road sign?
source_cards.back: A Crossroad sign warns of a four-way intersection where cross traffic may enter; a Side Road sign warns of a T intersection with traffic joining from left or right.

source_cards.front: What does a Merge sign warn of, and how does an Add Lane sign differ?

source_cards.front: What does a Lane Reduction sign tell drivers in the marked lane?
source_cards.back: A Lane Reduction sign means the marked lane ends soon and drivers in it must merge into the through lane.

source_cards.front: What does a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign tell you about your road?
source_cards.back: A Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign means your one-way road becomes a two-way road and you will meet oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: How does a Lane Reduction sign differ from a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign?
source_cards.back: A Lane Reduction sign means your lane is ending and you must merge, which differs from a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign, where a one-way road starts carrying oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow beacon on a pedestrian crossing sign mean?
source_cards.back: A pedestrian crossing sign may have a flashing yellow beacon, meaning someone is crossing now, has just crossed or is about to cross.

source_cards.front: What do the Multiuse Path Crossing and In-Street Pedestrian Crossing signs each tell you?
source_cards.back: A Multiuse Path Crossing sign marks where cyclists and walkers often cross; an In-Street Pedestrian Crossing sign means stop when someone is in the crosswalk.

source_cards.front: What does a Stop Ahead sign warn you of, and how do you respond?
source_cards.back: A Stop Ahead sign warns of a stop sign ahead, so slow down and get ready to stop.

source_cards.front: What do the Signal Ahead and Reduced Speed Limit Ahead signs each ask you to prepare for?
source_cards.back: A Signal Ahead sign means slow down and be prepared to stop for a traffic light, and a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign means prepare to slow to a lower limit.

source_cards.front: What does a Low Clearance sign mean for a tall vehicle?
source_cards.back: A Low Clearance sign means the overpass ahead is low, so do not continue if your vehicle is too tall to fit beneath it.

source_cards.front: What does a Hill sign warn you about?
source_cards.back: A Hill sign warns of a steep grade ahead.

source_cards.front: What do the Slippery When Wet and Deer signs warn of?
source_cards.back: A Slippery When Wet sign means the pavement becomes unusually slick in rain, and a Deer sign means deer often cross there, so slow down if you see deer or other wildlife.

source_cards.front: What do route signs tell you about the road you are on?
source_cards.back: Route signs tell you which road you are on and whether it is an interstate, a U.S. route or a state highway.

source_cards.front: What do green guide signs give you, and why does the exit number help?
source_cards.back: Green guide or information signs give exit details and point the way to roads and cities, and the exit number helps you choose the right exit.

source_cards.front: What do blue motorist service signs show?
source_cards.back: Blue motorist service signs show gas, food, lodging, rest areas, electric vehicle charging, accessible facilities or parking, and the way to a hospital.

source_cards.front: How do you handle a dark signal, and how do you handle a broken one that flashes?
source_cards.back: A dark signal, as in a power outage, means stop as if every approach had a stop sign; a broken signal that flashes yellow or red is obeyed by its flashing meaning.

source_cards.front: How do you treat a flashing red light or a dark signal?
source_cards.back: A flashing red light or a dark signal is treated exactly like a stop sign.

source_cards.front: How does a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
source_cards.back: A steady red light means stop and stay stopped until it changes, while a flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.

source_cards.front: After a complete stop on red, which turns may you make when nothing forbids them?
source_cards.back: After a complete stop on red, unless a sign or officer forbids it, you may turn right onto a two-way road, or turn right or left onto a one-way road in its direction of travel.

source_cards.front: When is a turn on red allowed to the right, and when to the left?

source_cards.front: At higher speeds, when may you pass a bicyclist in your lane?

source_cards.back: On snow or ice, press and release the brakes gently, since slamming them will likely send the vehicle into a skid.

source_cards.back: Take turns on snow or ice at a reduced, steady speed to avoid skidding.

source_cards.back: A skid happens when the tires can no longer grip the road, and driving too fast for conditions is what causes it.

source_cards.back: In a skid, stay off the brakes, because they will not work well until the vehicle slows.

source_cards.front: How do you steer out of a skid?
source_cards.back: In a skid, steer the way you want the vehicle to go, turn the wheel back as soon as it starts to straighten so it does not swing the other way, and keep correcting left and right until you are back in control.

source_cards.back: Snow and ice hide the road ahead and lengthen braking distance, so drive slower, leave more space, clear snow, ice and fog off the windows, and leave cruise control off.
